claims: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The splashdown marked the safe return of the first astronauts to journey around the moon in over 50 years.
The mission was returning from a lunar flyby.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft hit the atmosphere at nearly 24,000 miles per hour.
The crew was transported to the USS John P. Murtha for immediate medical evaluation.
The capsule and crew were recovered by a joint effort of NASA and U.S. Navy teams.
